title: Choose VoteAware's visual world
question: The roll assigned Election Ink & Ballot Ledger. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Election Ink & Ballot Ledger
options.lineage: Indian indelible voting ink, ballot papers, EVM button grids, official rubber-stamp seals
options.thesis: Every MP's record rendered as a stamped ballot ledger — the one indelible mark that proves you actually voted, now proving whether they delivered.
options.viewport: A single oversized ink-stamp grade slams onto a sample MP's name; below it a ballot-slip search field ('Find your constituency') marked in the same indelible purple as the stamp.
options.risk: Tips into gimmicky novelty if the stamp/ink motif is overused instead of reserved for verdicts.

raised.raise: Dense tables (MP list, fund ledger) use split-flap's cascading row-update rhythm and strict ruled-row/column discipline instead of ordinary rows.
Tapping any grade component draws a thin leader line to the exact fund-data row it came from — full traceability, borrowed as an annotation grammar only.
The scorecard's category summary doubles as a numbered map you navigate the page by, the way a bento box's lid diagram indexes its compartments.

regions.label: hero: oversized ink-stamp grade on sample MP
side rail: ballot-row ticker of sample MPs (name, party symbol, stamp grade)
trust strip: data-source counterfoil (MPLADS, PRS, ECI)

options.label: UPI Ledger
options.lineage: PhonePe/GPay transaction history and balance receipts
options.thesis: Your MP's public money, rendered exactly like the private money you check every day: debited, credited, balance.
options.viewport: A balance-style hero number (funds unspent) tops a receipt-style scrollable list of MPs, each row reading like a transaction: allotted / spent / balance.
options.risk: Also the direction most civic-fintech-adjacent apps in this category land on — immediately legible, but not distinctive against every payment app on a young voter's phone.

regions.label: balance-style hero: total unspent across tracked MPs
receipt list: MP rows as transaction entries

options.label: Concourse Departure Board
options.thesis: MPs ranked live like train departures — on-time, delayed, or cancelled, by fund utilization instead of platform.
options.case: Fuses cleanly for the ranked MP list and live-update states; loses to the assigned direction on identifying with voting/politics specifically — transit is a real but tangential association.
options.risk: Reads as a transit-app clone if the flap motif isn't reserved for genuine state changes.

options.label: Exploded Specification Sheet
options.lineage: Utility patent drawing sheets — numbered figures, leader lines, ink hatching
options.thesis: A grade exploded into its numbered parts, every figure tied by a leader line to the exact clause of spending it proves.
options.case: Fuses well with the product's traceability principle — strong product clarity for 'why this grade' — but the patent-office register is less culturally familiar to young Indian voters than ballot ephemera.
options.risk: Can feel cold/technical if the ink-line discipline isn't warmed by the ballot palette around it.

regions.label: exploded hero figure: grade broken into numbered parts

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The generic civic-dashboard look: tricolor accents, an official emblem, blue-and-white stat cards.
canonCard.viewport: The government-portal arrangement every visitor already expects, executed at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other civic-tech dashboard, including the andhbhakt project this app is modeled after — no memorable identity of its own.
